title: Governor of California

context.text: Open seat: Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is term-limited. Under California's top-two primary system, the two highest vote-getters on June 2, 2026 advance regardless of party; Xavier Becerra (D) received 28% and Steve Hilton (R) 25%.
Hilton finished ahead of Democrat Tom Steyer, who spent more than $200 million of his own money in the primary and later urged supporters to back Becerra.

candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.ballotNote: Top-two primary finisher (28%); one of two candidates on the official certified general-election list. California governors have no ballot-line running mate; the lieutenant governor is elected separately.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2021–2025) and California Attorney General (2017–2021)

summary.text: Xavier Becerra is a Democrat and former California attorney general, U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services and member of Congress (1993–2017). His campaign emphasizes lowering housing, utility and insurance costs and resisting Trump administration policies.

background.text: Born in Sacramento; B.A. in economics (1980) and J.D. (1984) from Stanford University.
Served in the California State Assembly (1990–1992) and the U.S. House of Representatives (1993–2017), including as chair of the House Democratic Caucus (2013–2017).
Appointed California Attorney General by Gov. Jerry Brown in 2017 and elected to a full term in 2018; U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services under President Biden, 2021–2025.

priorities.text: Declare a state of emergency to freeze insurance and utility rates and to fund 40,000 units of already-approved affordable housing.
Continue resisting Trump administration policies on issues such as immigration and the environment.
Expand state health coverage and lower costs, including by cutting insurers' administrative spending.

positions.summary: Would push cities to zone more residential land for apartments, duplexes and condos and crack down on cities that make it harder to build housing.
Supports California's sanctuary law, which he defended in court as attorney general.
Was a longtime supporter of single-payer health care and now supports expanding state coverage to as many residents as possible.
Supports a progressive income tax and extending a higher tax rate on high earners to pay for schools, but opposes Proposition 40, the billionaire wealth-tax measure.
Supports the state's clean-energy transition goals but is open to revising them, including the 2035 gas-car sales ban, if they make gas and energy unaffordable.

record.text: As California Attorney General, led a coalition of 20 states and D.C. in petitioning the U.S. Supreme Court to review the Fifth Circuit's decision in Texas v. U.S., which held the ACA's individual mandate unconstitutional.

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.ballotNote: Top-two primary finisher (25%); one of two candidates on the official certified general-election list; endorsed by President Donald Trump.
candidates.currentRole: Political commentator; former Fox News host

summary.text: Steve Hilton is a Republican political commentator who hosted 'The Next Revolution' on Fox News from 2017 to 2023 and was a policy adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron. His platform centers on income- and gas-tax cuts, loosening housing and environmental rules and changing the state's sanctuary law.

background.text: Born in London in 1969; studied Philosophy, Politics and Economics at New College, Oxford.
Served as director of strategy for UK Prime Minister David Cameron, 2010–2012; moved to California in 2012 and became a U.S. citizen in 2021.
Co-founded the crowd-funding platform Crowdpac and hosted Fox News's 'The Next Revolution' from 2017 to 2023.

priorities.text: Eliminate state income tax on the first $150,000 of earnings and halve the gas tax.
Lower gas prices by suspending environmental regulations and reduce regulation on housing construction.
Bring back the 'starter home' by cutting fees and building rules on smaller single-family homes and creating a state loan program for first-time buyers.

positions.summary: Wants to overturn California's sanctuary law limiting police cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
Wants to roll back California's climate rules mandating a clean-energy transition and allow more natural gas production.
Opposes Proposition 40, the one-time tax on billionaires' assets.
Supports using public funds to let parents in underperforming districts send their children to private schools or other districts.
Opposes the state law allowing transgender youth to compete on the school sports teams they choose.
Supports reducing restrictions on owning and using firearms.

researchNotes: The California Secretary of State's Official Certified List of Candidates for the November 3, 2026 general election (dated August 27, 2026) lists exactly two governor candidates, Xavier Becerra (Democratic) and Steve Hilton (Republican); this matches the guide. Ballotpedia was unreachable (bot challenge). Issue positions come from the CalMatters voter guide; neither campaign site published issue pages that could be retrieved, so no verbatim candidate quotes are included. A record item citing an HHS statement was removed because its archived page no longer loads and the official HHS page could not be retrieved. Becerra's House voting record and Hilton's campaign website content were not reviewed in depth. Running mates: California elects the lieutenant governor separately.
